title: Add RAG fuzz-authoring CLI and local replay proxy
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: onboarding teams frequently ask for a tiny, deterministic authoring loop to iterate retrieval+prompt mutations and catch regressions before hitting CI. This PR adds a lightweight authoring CLI (watch/fuzz mode) and a local replay proxy that records and replays RAG request/response traces for fast offline debugging and stepwise mutation testing. The intent is to give product engineers a low-friction way to reproduce retrieval-tooling interactions, run randomized prompt perturbations, and validate structured-output contracts locally.

What this PR delivers: 1) a new CLI under quickstarts/rag-authoring-cli that supports `watch`, `replay`, and `fuzz` subcommands; 2) a small browser-friendly replay proxy that can serve recorded sessions and simulate webhook/tool callbacks; 3) sample prompt mutation sets and a starter evaluation harness that runs headless fuzz iterations with pass/fail assertions; 4) docs and a quickstart README with step-by-step run commands and troubleshooting.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement watch/fuzz/replay CLI surface and examples
- [x] Add local replay proxy and adapter for tool callback simulation
- [x] Include sample corpora and mutation sets for common retrieval patterns
- [x] Provide README quickstart and troubleshooting section
- [x] Add lightweight telemetry probes (opt-in) to surface mismatch rates locally
- [x] Add unit tests and CI job for smoke coverage

Usage summary (quick): 
1) Start a local index (or use bundled sample) and run `yarn start` in quickstarts/rag-authoring-cli
2) In another shell run `node cli.js watch --profile=compact` to capture a session
3) Tweak prompt variants under samples/mutations and run `node cli.js fuzz --iterations=50` to run mutation-based checks
4) Use `node cli.js replay --session=last` to serve the recorded session to the browser shim or to a service under test

Notes on safety and privacy: recorded sessions are local by default and stored under ./sessions with a JSONL compression option; telemetry probes are opt-in and sanitized. See README for KMS/offline guidance for enterprise/private deployments.

Related links: Linear ENG-1887 (authoring loop), design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-1887/rag-authoring-cli (internal), docs page placeholder /docs/quickstarts/rag-authoring-cli.

Commits: single-squash history (see commits list below). CI: initial lint failure fixed in second commit; smoke tests and unit tests pass on rerun. Merge: squash-merged after approvals.

Files changed (high level): quickstarts/rag-authoring-cli/cli.js, quickstarts/rag-authoring-cli/README.md, quickstarts/rag-authoring-cli/proxy/replay-proxy.js, quickstarts/rag-authoring-cli/samples/mutations/*.json, quickstarts/rag-authoring-cli/tests/*, docs/quickstarts/rag-authoring-cli.md, package.json (dev deps).

Impact: developer UX improvement for local RAG iteration; no breaking API changes. Recommended follow-ups: a) incorporate into the docs site navigation, b) add a small demo to the examples gallery, c) expand fuzz mutation library with dataset contributions.
